items.name: 3-year note auction ($58bn, 11-09): high yield 4.627%, 0.5 bp tail vs WI 4.622%, bid-to-cover 2.53 (lowest since Aug 2025), indirects 55.5% (15-month low), directs record 35.0%, dealers 9.5%
items.headline: 3-year note auction ($58bn, 11-09): high yield 4.627%, 0.5 bp tail vs WI 4.622%, bid-to-cover 2.53 (lowest since Aug 2025), indirects 55.5% (15-month low), directs record 35.0%, dealers 9.5%
items.source: Investing.com (11-09 14:34), PrimeXBT (11-09), louisvelazquez.com auction recap (11-09), HERE Columbia (11-10), RTTNews (11-09); all read by WebFetch
items.claim: The Treasury sold $58bn of 3-year notes on 2026-11-09 at a high yield of 4.627%, 0.5 bp above the 4.622% when-issued level (average of prior auctions: 0.1 bp stop-through), with a bid-to-cover of 2.53 (average 2.64; lowest since the August 2025 refunding), indirect takedown 55.5% (average 62.7%; lowest in fifteen months), a record direct takedown of 35.0% (average 25.2%) and dealers 9.5% (average 12.1%); one recap grades it C-. Last month's 3-year stopped at 4.932% with a 2.62 bid-to-cover.
items.note: Tail of 0.5 bp is below the 2 bp hard-event threshold. Averages and the WI level are from a single recap (louisvelazquez.com). RTTNews prints 4.637% (outlier); a Gokhshtein copy of the ZeroHedge write-up says '2.5 bp tail, largest since May' (treated as garbled; ZeroHedge not readable). Investing.com says dealers were 0.8 sigma below their one-year average. 10-year ($42bn) is 11-10 and 30-year ($25bn) 11-12.

items.name: NextDC pauses all data-centre projects without customer contracts after M3 Melbourne suspension (Reuters)
items.headline: NextDC pauses all data-centre projects without customer contracts after M3 Melbourne suspension (Reuters)
items.source: Reuters (Christine Chen, Sydney), republished by The Star (Malaysia) and The Edge Malaysia; read by WebFetch
items.claim: On 2026-11-09 NextDC CEO Craig Scroggie told the UBS Australasia conference that the company has paused work on every project without a customer contract ('anything that didn't have a customer contract' is 'no longer a priority'), after power delays and community backlash suspended its flagship M3 Melbourne expansion and forced an earnings-forecast cut last month that removed about A$140m of contracted FY2027 revenue; shares fell 42% on the cut. NextDC had 11 data centres in development or planning per its 2026 annual report; Goodman and Digital Realty last week bought a 9.9% stake for A$715m.
items.note: No MW/GW figure for the paused projects; the company did not say how many are affected. The M3 suspension and guidance cut (October) predate the gate; the in-gate event is the stated pause of all uncontracted projects. The A$140m figure is from a secondary summary (shattered.io, citing ABC News and a company announcement). Scroggie called the situation 'probably reflective of the global environment'.

items.name: Morgan Stanley: 20% of US data center projects planned for 2028 (~5 GW) expected to slip to 2029 after midterms; hyperscaler capex forecasts unchanged at $1.6tn/$1.8tn
items.headline: Morgan Stanley: 20% of US data center projects planned for 2028 (~5 GW) expected to slip to 2029 after midterms; hyperscaler capex forecasts unchanged at $1.6tn/$1.8tn
items.source: investingLive (Adam Button) summary of the Morgan Stanley note 'Buy the Drop: AI Investment Opportunities Post the US Midterms'; corroborated by KuCoin/ChainThink (11-10) and 456X Evening Brief Nov 9; read by WebFetch
items.claim: In a note dated 2026-11-09 Morgan Stanley said it expects 20% of US data center projects planned for 2028, representing about 5 GW of capacity (roughly 10% of the global pipeline), to be delayed to 2029 rather than cancelled, mainly in Texas and Ohio where new governors could add construction requirements; US capacity additions would fall 4% in 2028 then rise 38% in 2029, while the bank keeps hyperscaler capex at $1.6tn for 2027 and $1.8tn for 2028 and sees a more than 30% shortage of powered capacity persisting through 2028.
items.note: Partial: a bank projection, not an announced deferral, and read via a secondary summary (note itself not seen; analysts unnamed). Projects already under construction are not expected to be disrupted. The bank flags supplier risk of slower orders and inventory build in 2028. Distinct from the 456X Nov 7 '11 GW could face pauses' estimate recorded 11-09 (different source and figure).

items.candidate_dial: pulled deal (neocloud: CRWV) - precursor only; secondary-market stress, no deal pulled
items.claim: As of 2026-11-09 some CoreWeave 2031 bonds yielded above 16% and its five-year CDS traded above 1,240 bp, up about 50% in a month, against $5.5bn cash and $35bn debt at end-June (bonds: $1.3bn 15% due March 2028, $3.2bn 11% due August 2030); CEO Mike Intrator said the company does not anticipate any impact to existing customer commitments, and IREN co-CEO Daniel Roberts said 'capital markets have become more selective in the last few weeks'. Investment-grade tech spreads are cited at about 110 bp in November versus about 80 bp in October.
